cases.name: explicit slash invocation
assertions: Obtains the waybill path from `session-guard.cjs handoff-path` and writes the waybill there, outside the repo, rather than into the repo root
Arms the handoff via `session-guard.cjs handoff-arm --kind waybill --waybill <absolute path>` using an absolute path, and does not hand-write a provenance stamp
Prints the absolute waybill path and tells the user to type /clear to start the fresh session themselves

cases.name: natural language wrap-up
cases.prompt: Let's wrap up and start fresh with a clean context window without losing where we are.
assertions: Recognizes the intent to reset context while preserving state
Captures task, status, next steps, key files, decisions, and git state
Does not attempt to run /clear itself — leaves that to the user

cases.name: committed checkpoint variant
assertions: Writes to docs/ferry/waybill-<timestamp>.md instead of the out-of-tree default location
Does not add the file to .git/info/exclude
Arms the handoff with `--owned false` so the committed checkpoint is never auto-deleted
Notes the user will want to commit the checkpoint

cases.name: here variant
assertions: Writes waybill.md in the repo root
Appends the line `waybill.md # mad-skills:ferry` to .git/info/exclude so cleanup can later remove exactly that line
Arms the handoff via `handoff-arm --kind waybill --waybill <absolute path>`

cases.name: clean mode dry run first
assertions: Runs `session-guard.cjs handoff-clean` without --yes first (dry run) and shows the listed owned waybills to the user
Asks the user before re-running with --yes to delete
Does not use --legacy unless the user asks or confirms
